headline: Highest risk is data leakage: caveman’s MCP/file surfaces can expose workspace data, while awesome-prompts is a non-runnable prompt repository with no direct write or network path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman exposes MCP and file surfaces (CLAUDE.md, project notes), so if awesome-prompts content is copied into those channels it can be treated as instructions. awesome-prompts itself is a prompt repository, not a runnable agent, so the bridge is indirect rather than default. The pathway exists, but only through user-mediated transfer.
conditions: IF content from awesome-prompts is pasted into caveman-managed files or MCP-fed context
IF caveman treats repository text as authoritative instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep awesome-prompts content out of CLAUDE.md and project notes
Add a manual review step before copying prompts into caveman
Use a separate scratch file for imported prompts
Mark imported prompt text as untrusted in the workflow

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents are docs-only and network_egress is none, so there is no direct exfiltration path. caveman touches session logs, memory files, and project notes, while awesome-prompts is a content-writing repository; leakage is mainly local workspace exposure if they share files. The blast radius is limited and no third-party upload is indicated.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same local workspace
IF sensitive notes are stored in caveman-managed memory files or project notes
mitigations: Store sensitive notes outside the shared workspace
Separate the two agents into different directories
Review memory files before reuse
Disable copying session logs into shared docs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-prompts has no write or concurrency surfaces, while caveman supports multiple instances and file-based project artifacts. That means there is little direct write-write conflict between the pair; any conflict would come from the operator placing both on the same mutable files. The overlap is limited and not dangerous by default.
conditions: IF the operator points both agents at the same writable directory
IF caveman instances edit the same project notes or CLAUDE.md concurrently
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Avoid concurrent edits to shared files
Use one caveman instance per workspace
Back up files before multi-agent edits

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman can consume files and project notes, so if awesome-prompts output is imported, caveman may treat it as guidance without verification. awesome-prompts is a prompt-writing source, not a validator, so the pair can propagate unvetted instructions into downstream work. The pathway exists in default documentation workflows, though not as an autonomous action chain.
conditions: IF awesome-prompts text is used as input to caveman workflows
IF caveman executes or rewrites based on imported prompt content without review
mitigations: Require human review of imported prompts
Tag imported content as non-authoritative
Use a checklist before downstream execution
Keep source prompts separate from operational notes

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. The only compliance-relevant surface is caveman’s session logs, memory files, and project notes; awesome-prompts is a public prompt repository. Because the pair does not show a cross-border or regulated-data pathway, this is a limited documentation-gap risk rather than a breach scenario.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in caveman session logs or memory files
IF those files are then copied into public prompt repositories
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in session logs
Keep memory files local and access-controlled
Review files before publishing or sharing
Use separate repositories for public prompts and private notes
